The opclasses argument of django.contrib.postgres.constraints.ExclusionConstraint is deprecated in favor of using django.contrib.postgres.indexes.OpClass in .ExclusionConstraint.expressions. To use it, you need to add 'django.contrib.postgres' in your INSTALLED_APPS. After making this change, makemigrations will generate a new migration with two operations: RemoveConstraint and AddConstraint. Since this change has no effect on the database schema, the django.db.migrations.operations.SeparateDatabaseAndState operation can be used to only update the migration state without running any SQL. Move the generated operations into the state_operations argument of django.db.migrations.operations.SeparateDatabaseAndState. For example:: class Migration(migrations.Migration): ... operations = [ migrations.SeparateDatabaseAndState( database_operations=[], state_operations=[ migrations.RemoveConstraint(...), migrations.AddConstraint(...), ], ), ]
